aggressive_definition: Advanced, lethal, and high-grade incident prostate cancer outcomes.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: Clinical features of prostate cancer included advanced, lethal and high-grade outcomes.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: A total of 48,137 men from the Health Professionals Follow-up Study were followed from 1986 to 2017.
reason: The prospective cohort analyzed both overall incident prostate cancer and aggressive incident subtypes. The abstract reports 7,108 total cases, including 564 advanced cases, and separately reports 1,065 lethal cases; the aggressive case-count field records the advanced endpoint corresponding to the supplied estimate.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Compared to never-users, men who used multivitamin 10 or more tablets per week had similar risk of advanced (HR: 1.14, 95% CI: 0.77-1.70, P<sub>trend</sub>=0.46) or lethal (HR: 1.07, 95% CI: 0.80-1.44, P<sub>trend</sub>=0.59) prostate cancer, and multivitamin use of 15 years or more was not associated with risk of advanced (HR: 1.10, 95% CI: 0.80-1.50, P<sub>trend</sub>=0.46) or lethal (HR: 1.04, 95% CI: 0.83-1.31, P<sub>trend</sub>=0.13) prostate cancer.
estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied HR of 1.14 compares at least 10 tablets per week with never use for incident advanced prostate cancer, an explicitly aggressive endpoint.
